D01.observed: Direct labels and a matched trained-token output were tested. The Qwen browser path passed a two-message smoke. A separate two-output BERT export preserved all 100 decisions in actual browser execution. A shared two/four-layer browser model also matches every saved exit; typed input loads only its 44.5 MB adaptive graphs.
D01.remaining: No reliable enum-only timing advantage or general output-format superiority.

D02.observed: Fixed early, middle, late and full-depth classifiers compared; all four actual stopping depths timed over three paired passes.
D02.remaining: No general layer at which arbitrary answers become ready.

D03.observed: Actual input-dependent exits execute in Python and the browser. On 500 unused messages, the original shared BERT rule proposes 400 layer-2 exits and preserves all full-depth decisions, projecting 40% fewer blocks. Its model gets 440/500 correct. The selected distilled model gets 451/500 but increases toxic misses from 3 to 5; its learned risk check stops fewer cases than the confidence rule.
D03.remaining: Actual reliability beyond this eligible annotated remainder is unproven: only18 toxic cases, with wide rare-error bounds. Full-depth errors remain. No general or deployment-safety acceptance claim.

D04.observed: Changing-rule and unfamiliar-input tests expose failures.
D04.remaining: No demonstrated arbitrary instruction following or long-conversation robustness.

D05.observed: Actual layer traces and request times measured. Fixed-prefix reuse and four-message batches preserved all 100 predictions while reducing own paired workload times by 37.9% and 9.7%; every message still uses all 24 layers. Combined prefix reuse+batch4 reduced its paired50-message workload by42.9%, preserving all decisions; all24 layers execute. Original shared BERT saved 34.7% in three actual CPU passes on the first50 fresh messages, preserving predictions and layer traces; a separate consumed50 browser test saved36.4% with real shared-state continuation. Loading is excluded and separately reported.
D05.remaining: Independent hardware, cold starts, live arrival queues and broader quality replication remain untested.

D06.observed: Original cascade and conservative follow-up tested on 100 unused messages. Strict version preserved decisions but avoided Qwen only twice and saved less than 1% time.
D06.remaining: No useful quality-preserving speed improvement established by the conservative follow-up; broader datasets and error-budget validation remain.

C02.observed: Earlier ScreenSpot region selection found 25/30 present targets. On a fresh OSWorld-G stress test, it found 8/25 present targets. A frozen confidence cutoff withheld all 25 author-labelled infeasible requests, but allowed only 4 present requests: 2 correct and 2 wrong. Predicted-point cropping improved 2/10 to 3/10 with another complete model pass.
C02.remaining: Useful click coverage and reliable accepted actions remain unresolved. The new domain test does not establish strict application-family disjointness or literal missing-control detection; infeasible requests can include impossible actions on present controls.

C03.observed: Coordinate model still runs all 28 transformer blocks.
C03.remaining: Needs trained intermediate pointer heads and reliable grounding/abstention controls.
